name: Maelstrom
turf: Northside Industrial District, northern Kabuki, the Hot Zone, Old Japantown edges
look: Exposed chrome, red optics, leather, cables, the gang mark etched into metal
leader: Warlock (2045) · Royce and Brick (2077, All Foods plant)
origin: Maelstrom is what crawled out of three funerals. In the late 2010s the Metal Warriors were a Combat Zone boostergang that treated flesh as a first draft. The Inquisitors nearly erased them for the sin of chrome. Survivors, plus leftovers from the Iron Sights and the Red Chrome Legion, welded themselves into a new name: Maelstrom — a word that means you do not swim out. By 2020 they were already a rumor with a body count. By 2045 Warlock had turned the rumor into a syndicate: smuggling, extortion, hired murder, and a philosophy that meat is a warranty problem. By 2077 they own the All Foods plant in Northside and the Totentanz, and the street still flinches when red eyes catch a headlamp.
text:
A Maelstrom ganger is easy to spot and hard to talk down. They install until the human outline is a suggestion: wolvers, skinweave, optics that never blink, pain editors that make interrogation a waste of time. Cyberpsychosis is not a warning label for them. It is a promotion track. The gang sells smash, Black Lace, stolen military chrome, and the kind of heist that ends with a warehouse full of holes.

They do not hold turf the way Valentinos do. They hold industrial wreckage and dare anyone to want it. NCPD writes them off as a MaxTac problem. Trauma Team will not land without a paid corridor. Edgerunners who take a Maelstrom gig should assume the client is also the ambush.

The name is the creed. Once you are in the whirlpool, the only way out is as parts.
hooks: Warlock (or Royce) wants a crate of milspec chrome lifted from a Militech lockup before Inquisitors torch it.
A ganger is mid-cyberpsycho break in Northside. MaxTac is eight minutes out. The party is closer.
Someone etched the Maelstrom mark on a Forlorn Hope regular. The Hope wants the name, not a war.

name: Tyger Claws
turf: Japantown, Kabuki, Charter Hill, Little China edges, Watson Development
look: Embroidered jackets, reflex chrome, katanas, bikes, jewelry or tattoos of the claw
leader: Hayato / Shinobu the Second (2045) · Jun Azegami and cell bosses (2077)
origin: They started as a Japantown protector crew in the 2010s: kids with martial arts, cheap boosters, and Arasaka money in the background. The 2020 street called them Tyger's Claw. They kept Japanese families safe from the Combat Zone spillover and collected for the privilege. After the Fourth Corporate War, Arasaka's leash slipped. Hayato took more chrome to dull the pain of an empire that would not sit still, and Maelstrom tried to eat Old Japantown. The Claws did not give it to them. By 2077 they are the largest street gang in the city — five thousand plus — running clubs, dens, casinos, and the kind of protection that comes with a bill and a blade.
text:
Tyger Claws look like a night out until they do not. They own more legitimate fronts than any other crew: karaoke, noodles, bikes, rooms you should not ask the hourly rate of. Under the lanterns it is yakuza math. Honor is a costume they wear in front of the block and take off in the back room.

They prefer speed — Sandevistan, bikes, katanas — over the full-borg religion of Maelstrom. That does not make them gentle. The Mox exist because Claws killed Lizzie Borden and decided the lesson was not finished. Wakako Okada has made a career out of being the fixer who can still pick up a Claw phone.

If you work Japantown, you pay them, you join them, or you leave before last call.
hooks: A Kabuki club wants the party to retrieve a stolen Kendachi blade before the Claws notice it moved.
Hayato (or a 2077 cell boss) will pay outsiders to hit a Maelstrom chop-shop his people cannot be seen near.
A Mox runner asks for proof that a Claw lieutenant ordered a beating. Proof is rarer than the beating.

name: Valentinos
turf: Heywood, the Glen, Vista del Rey, Santo Domingo edges
look: Gold, roses, saints, lowriders, church candles, family ink
leader: Padre and block captains (2045–2077) · family tables, not a single throne
origin: The Valentinos grew out of Heywood's Latino neighborhoods when the city still pretended those streets had a police department. In the 2010s they were already a family gang: protection, pride, a dress code, and a church calendar. The 2020 books spelled them Valentino's. The apostrophe fell off. The rules did not. They survived the Fourth Corporate War by being the one crew that still buried its dead with a priest in the room. By 2045 Padre was the quiet center of gravity. By 2077 they are Heywood's other government — honor, vendetta, lowriders, and a punishment for every sin that has a name.
text:
Valentinos will feed you, dance with you, and kill you for disrespecting a cousin. They are not Maelstrom. They have mothers and saints and a sense of the block as a living thing. That makes them more dangerous in their own zip code, not less. Outsiders who treat them like a booster gang learn that the gold is not costume jewelry.

They run cars, protection, street pharmacies, and the kind of funeral that shuts a whole avenue. Jackie Welles came out of this water. So did a lot of people who never got a drink named after them.

6th Street shares Heywood and pretends that makes them neighbors. It does not.
hooks: Padre wants a stolen lowrider returned before a funeral. The thieves are 6th Street kids who thought it was a joke.
A Valentino cousin took a gig in Pacifica and did not come back. The family will pay for a body or a name.
A church on the Glen is being taxed by a new crew. The Valentinos will not fire first in a nave. They will hire someone who will.

name: 6th Street
turf: Vista del Rey, the Glen, North Heywood, Rancho Coronado, Little Europe edges
look: NUSA surplus, faded flags, block-watch armor, militia haircuts
leader: Solomon "X" Wright and veteran captains (2045) · militia councils (2077)
origin: 6th Street was born from people who came home from the Fourth Corporate War and found NCPD was a rumor with a badge. Veterans in Vista del Rey stacked sandbags, issued radios, and told the block they were the law now. In 2045 they still looked like a neighborhood watch that had gotten into surplus crates. By the Unification War they had practiced being an army. By 2077 the watch is a racket: checkpoints, smuggling, 'security' contracts, and a patriotic brand that covers a lot of graves.
text:
They will tell you they protect Heywood. Sometimes they do. They also shake down the same bodegas they 'saved,' run guns, and pick fights with Valentinos over whose mural stays on which wall. The surplus gear is real. So is the veteran skill. So is the slide from guardian gang to PMC that forgot who hired it.

Davis Squad and other cells have their own grudges. Treat 6th Street as one animal and you will be surprised by the teeth in the next alley.

If a checkpoint asks for papers in Heywood, smile. If they ask for your chrome serials, you are already in a scene.
hooks: X Wright wants proof a Militech stash is feeding Maelstrom, not the block.
A 6th Street checkpoint 'lost' a nomad convoy's papers. The Aldecaldos will pay to get the people back.
A veteran in the Willows says 6th Street is recruiting her patients as muscle. She wants it stopped quietly.

name: Voodoo Boys
status: Active (two different crews have worn the name)
turf: 2045: Pacifica Playground, Rancho Coronado drug corners · 2077: Pacifica, the Grand Imperial wreck, the Old NET
look: 2045 posers in Hollywood 'voodoo' fashion · 2077 netrunners in white, veves, decks, and silence
leader: Baron D (2045 posers) · Placide and the houngans (2077 Pacifica nation)
origin: The name is a theft that became a nation. In 2020 and still in 2045, a poser/drug crew draped itself in Hollywood voodoo, sold product, and lost ground to the Piranhas. They were violent tourists. The Haitian community in Pacifica — the people who actually had rites, language, and a reason to hide — took the insult and outlived it. After the Fourth Corporate War and the collapse of the Old NET, Pacifica's netrunners built a church out of ice and black ice. By 2077 the Voodoo Boys are not a fashion. They are the only crew that treats the Blackwall as a door instead of a fence, and they will kill a tourist for knocking.
text:
Do not confuse the 2045 posers with the 2077 nation. The posers mug, deal, and dress for a camera. The Pacifica Boys run the NET the way a houngan runs a rite: initiation, secrecy, and a body if you talk. They hired outsiders only when the job would get a citizen killed. They burn the outsiders after.

Animals share Pacifica and want the mall. The Boys want the cables under the mall. That war is still on the map.

If a client says they can get you past the Blackwall, they are lying, or they are a Voodoo Boy, or you are already dead.
hooks: A 2045 Baron D wants a Piranha shoal embarrassed, not killed. The embarrassment should make the news.
A 2077 houngan needs a meat body to walk into a corp icebox their runners cannot physically enter.
Someone in the party has a Haitian grandmother's veve as a tattoo. A Pacifica runner wants to know why.

name: Animals
turf: Pacifica, Santo Domingo gyms, the Grand Imperial Mall, underground fight circuits
look: Combat-drug muscle, tank tops, veins, little chrome compared to the mass
leader: Pack bosses and pit promoters, not a single king
origin: The Animals are a 2070s answer to a city that sells strength in a syringe. They grew out of Santo Domingo gyms, Pacifica wrecks, and the underground fight economy — people who decided the next evolution was not a neural link but a body that could throw a car. They are boosters who mostly skip the obvious metal and go for grafted tissue, hormones, and the kind of 'dorphs that make a heart a countdown. By 2077 they own pits in the Grand Imperial Mall and a turf war with the Voodoo Boys that is less ideology than gravity: two big animals in one ruined district.
text:
You do not out-box an Animal. You out-think one, or you bring a gun and a plan for the second Animal behind you. They run fights, muscle jobs, and the drug pipeline that keeps the pits full. Close combat is a religion. Smartguns are for people who missed leg day.

They are not stupid. Promoters who last a year can count. Packs that last five years can read a contract. Treat them like dumb meat and you become the undercard.

Pacifica at night is their gym. The mall is the locker room. The street is the ring.
hooks: A pit boss wants a ringer to throw a fight without looking like they threw it.
Voodoo Boys paid to have an Animal pack's juice cut with something that causes heart failure. The pack wants the chemist.
A Santo gym is 'recruiting' with broken kneecaps. The owner will pay for a week of peace.

name: The Mox
turf: Kabuki, Lizzie's Bar, Watson's working doors
look: Pink and electric hair, bats, patched jackets, heart-and-bat iconography
leader: The memory of Anna Nox and Lizzie Borden · bar captains at Lizzie's
origin: The Mox are new by Night City standards and old by the standards of people who work doors. Anna 'Mox' Nox started a crew to keep sex workers from being the city's cheapest punching bag. Tyger Claws killed Lizzie Borden and several of her people and expected the lesson to stick. It stuck the other way. By 2077 Lizzie's Bar is a chapel, an armory, and a hiring hall. The Mox are small. They are not soft. They remember names.
text:
They protect working girls and guys, run braindance rooms, and keep a list of Claw faces that does not get shorter. They will hire edgerunners who can hit a den without turning Kabuki into a war the Mox cannot win. They will not hire edgerunners who talk about the clients.

If you want a safe room in Watson, this is one of the few that is not a trap. If you want to slum in Lizzie's for atmosphere, read the room. The bats are not decor.
hooks: A Claw lieutenant who was at Lizzie's the night she died is drinking in Charter Hill. The Mox want him walking, not famous.
A BD wreath in the back room has a recording the Mox cannot decrypt. They will pay a netrunner who can keep a secret.
A working kid from Pacifica asks for Mox colors. The bar wants a background check that does not go through NCPD.

name: Scavengers
turf: No flag. Hot Zone wrecks, Combat Zone alleys, anywhere a body still has chrome
look: Filthy raincoats, surgical masks, vans, plastic sheeting, stolen optics
leader: Crew bosses. There is no council. That is the point.
origin: In 2045 a scavver is a classification: small crews picking the Hot Zone and the junkyards for salvage that will not scream. By 2077 the worst of them organized into harvest gangs. They do not want your wallet. They want your linear frame, your second heart, your eyes. Night City taught them that Trauma Team only lands for a card, so a sleeper in a wreck is a buffet. The street shortened the name to scavs and started locking doors from the inside.
text:
A scavver in 2045 might sell you a decent generator and a story. A scav in 2077 will sell your kidneys to a body bank before the story is finished. The overlap is real. The difference is whether the crew still pretends the chrome was already detached.

They have no turf because turf is a place you sleep. They have routes, vans, and ripperdocs who do not ask. If a van idles at the end of an alley with the side door open, you are not looking at a delivery.
hooks: A ripper in Watson is buying 'fresh' optics that still have a serial from a living client.
The party finds a marked wreck in the Hot Zone. The mark is tonight.
A scav crew stole a Trauma Team crash cart. The Team will not file a report. They will hire.

name: Barghest
turf: Dogtown — the walled Pacifica exclusion, Hansen's city-state
look: Milspec patches, skull motifs, checkpoints, yellow-and-black hazard, stolen NUSA kit
origin: Barghest is what happens when a warlord is handed a district and a leftover army. After the Unification War, Kurt Hansen took the abandoned NUSA expeditionary force, the walls, and Pacifica's forgotten stadium district and declared a new law: his. Dogtown is not a gang turf. It is a city with one gang. Barghest runs the checkpoints, the black market under the stadium, the AV corridor, and the firing squads. Night City pretends the wall is someone else's problem. It is Hansen's product.
text:
You do not join Barghest the way you join 6th Street. You enlist, you buy a pass, or you die on the wrong side of a painted line. They have ranks, radios, and a logistics chain stolen from a national army. Street kids who wear a Barghest patch without the paperwork last as long as the next patrol.

If your table is in Dogtown, Barghest is the weather. If your table is outside the wall, Barghest is the rumor that buys prototype chrome and sells it back to the city that built the wall.
hooks: A pass into Dogtown expires at dawn. Hansen's people will extend it for a job that cannot have Barghest fingerprints.
A prototype from the stadium black market is walking. Hansen wants it back quieter than a firefight.
Someone inside Barghest wants out. Out is a hole in the wall and a list of names they are willing to sell.

name: Wraiths
turf: Badlands around Night City, highway cuts, wreck-farms
look: Spiked buggies, dusty leathers, bone and chrome fetishes, night-running lights
leader: Clan bosses. No office. No phone tree.
origin: Wraiths are the Badlands' answer to a city that still thinks the desert is empty. They are a Raffen Shiv strain: nomads who were exiled from the nations for the kind of crime even a pack will not carry. They raid convoys, strip wrecks, and treat Aldecaldo camps as a pantry. By 2077 they are the reason a night drive to the city is a scene, not a commute.
text:
They are not a street gang. They are a weather system with engines. A Wraith pack will run you off the asphalt, take the CHOOH2, and leave the bodies where the next pack can see the lesson. Aldecaldos hate them the way ranchers hate a fire that thinks it is a neighbor.

If your table leaves the metro, put Wraiths on the random encounter table and mean it.
hooks: An Aldecaldo panzer never arrived. The wreck is still warm. The Wraiths who hit it took a kid, not just fuel.
A corp convoy wants desert muscle that is not nomad-nation. They will regret this. The party can be the regret or the invoice.
A Wraith scout is dying of a bioplague in a culvert and will trade a camp location for a medkit.

name: Aldecaldos
status: Active (nation, not a street gang — still on this list because Night City treats them as one)
turf: Badlands camps east and south of the metro, mobile
look: Family panzers, sun-faded jackets, camp tattoos, working chrome
leader: Clan heads (Saul in the 2077 Night City camp, among others)
origin: The Aldecaldos are one of the great nomad nations, older than most of the buildings that sneer at them. They were not founded to mug Heywood. They were founded to leave a country that had stopped being a country. Night City still files them under 'gang' because the NCPD form only has so many boxes. They run salvage, escort, smuggling, and the last honest mechanic culture in a hundred klicks of dust.
text:
An Aldecaldo camp is a town that can move. They will hire edgerunners who keep their word. They will exile edgerunners who treat the camp like a pit stop with a bar. Wraiths are the enemy. Corps are the weather. The city is a market you enter in daylight and leave before the wall cameras learn your plates.

If you need a family that is not a Valentino sermon and not a 6th Street flag, this is the one. Do not call them a gang to their face unless you like walking home.
hooks: The camp needs a part that only exists in a Santo chop-shop. The shop is Maelstrom-adjacent.
A young Aldecaldo wants out of the desert and into the Afterlife. The clan wants them talked out of it, or followed.
Wraiths hit a water tanker. The next one leaves at dusk. They want guns that can keep up.

name: The Bozos
status: Active in splinter circuses; a Night City tradition nobody asked to keep
turf: Citywide. Circuses claim buses, ice-cream trucks, and whatever block they ruin this week.
look: Full clown bodysculpt. You will not mistake them.
leader: Multiple circus bosses after Hilaria 2045 (Great Bozo, Blammo, Jester, Dead Ringer…)
origin: They appeared in West Hill around 2017 as a prankster gang with circus chrome: red noses, rictus smiles, the whole cursed poster. Night City laughed. Then the pranks started removing fingers, then families, then city blocks. By 2020 they were a terrorism story with a honk. The Fourth Corporate War did not kill the joke. In 2045 a festival called Hilaria split them into at least thirteen circuses, now at war with each other in the only language they have. The Inquisitors hate them. Everyone else just runs.
text:
A Bozo is a poser who crossed the line into cult. Exotic bodysculpt, bike horns, squirt guns full of things that are not water, school buses with ramming plates. They will torture for timing. They will kill for a punchline. Civil war between circuses is not a relief. It is two clowns in your living room.

Philharmonic Vampyres think they are artists. Bozos think artists are props. Julliard crosses the street.
hooks: Two circuses have scheduled a 'show' in the same plaza. The Chamber of Commerce will pay to make it not happen.
A Dead Ringer stole a kid. The other Dead Ringer (different hair) says it wasn't them. Someone is lying in greasepaint.
An Inquisitor cell wants Bozo chrome peeled. They will not pay in cash. They will pay in a name.

name: Inquisitors
turf: Nowhere and everywhere. White hoodies in a crowd.
look: White hoodies, gas masks, jewelry etched with the mark, almost no chrome
leader: Unknown. Cells are built so torture does not map the church.
origin: The Inquisitors are older than Maelstrom and they would like credit for the body count. They believe cyberware is a sin you can tear out of a person with a pair of pliers and a hymn. In the 2010s they nearly annihilated the Metal Warriors and made a hobby of hunting boosters. Blood Razors put a bounty on their leader. It did not end them. By 2045 they still operate in cells, still wear the hoodie, still carry microwavers and EMP, still think a chrome arm is a confession.
text:
They are not street clowns. They are a cult with operational security. A cell can be your coworker, your trauma-team nurse, your landlord. They target chrome users, ripperdocs, and the occasional corpo who thinks a hidden holster is subtle.

Maelstrom is the theological enemy. That does not make Inquisitors the heroes. A party with obvious implants is a sermon waiting to happen.
hooks: A ripperdoc's chair was stripped of tools and the last patient is missing an arm that was not scheduled.
An Inquisitor hoodie was found in a 6th Street locker. X Wright wants it handled before the block becomes a crusade.
A cell offers the party a job on a Maelstrom chop-shop. Payment is 'absolution.' Read that twice.

name: Iron Sights
turf: Old Combat Zone, Old Japantown edges
look: Mohawks, punk leathers, facial scarification, old-school booster chrome
leader: BloodGuts, with fixer Hornet as the new money
origin: Classic Combat Zone booster gang: turf, mohawks, and a long memory of being almost eaten by history. They lost people to Maelstrom's founding and spent years in a knife fight with the Red Chrome Legion. In 2045 a fixer named Hornet put real backing behind BloodGuts and the Sights stopped being a nostalgia act. They still look like 2020. They hit like someone paid the ammo bill.
text: If you want a gang that still believes in holding a street corner with a pipe, this is the one. They run theft, drugs, sex work, and extortion the old way. Red Chrome Legion is the war that never ended. Maelstrom is the cousin who made it. Hornet is the reason they have grenades again.
hooks: Hornet wants a Red Chrome gas-mask cache stolen, not destroyed. BloodGuts wants it burned. The party is the tie-breaker.
An Old Japantown shop paid both Sights and Claws. Both noticed.
A kid with a new mohawk says they were jumped in. The Sights say they were not.

name: Red Chrome Legion
status: Active, at war with Iron Sights
turf: Little China, Old Japantown
look: Gas masks with glowing red lenses, hate-group theater, cheap pistols
leader: Vox and Populi, preaching a 'Great Caesar'
origin: A neo-nazi combat cult that has been a stain on Night City since the 2020 books. They talk about a messiah who will rise from their ranks and 'cleanse' the metro. They have been in a war of attrition with the Iron Sights so long that some street kids think the war is the gang. Maelstrom took some of their leftovers when the Metal Warriors died. The Legion did not get kinder.
text: They mug, extort, and hunt people who do not fit the sermon. Gold Dragons and Tyger Claws share zip codes and do not share patience. If your table wants a villain with no romance, put red lenses on them and do not give them a redemption arc.
hooks: A Little China shopkeeper paid Gold Dragons for protection. The Legion still came. Eddy Sing wants a message.
Vox and Populi are splitting over who gets to be Caesar. A fixer will pay to pick a winner, or neither.
Someone is selling Legion masks to poser kids in Kabuki. The real Legion will not find that funny.

name: Philharmonic Vampyres
turf: University District, tunnels under the symphony hall, citywide pranks
look: Goth evening wear, capes, fangs (some chrome, some sculpt), theater makeup
leader: The Master (goth/art faction) and Acme (prankster faction)
origin: They began as a prankster gang. In 2010 a bit involving tuxedos, capes, and fangs landed so hard that half the crew never took the costume off. They nested under the performing-arts halls, which puts them in occasional knife-range of Arasaka security and in permanent feud with street mimes — and therefore with Julliard. By 2045 the gang has a split personality that somehow still shares a rehearsal space.
text: The Master's people stage productions and expensive jokes aimed at rockerboys and corpos who can afford the cleanup. Acme's people want the old chaotic bit back. Rank and file of both factions get along. Leadership does not. They are rarely lethal. They are often career-ending. Do not hire them as muscle. Hire them as a problem for someone else's evening.
hooks: The Master wants a corpo premiere ruined without blood. Acme wants blood. The party is the director.
Julliard mimes have been disappearing into the symphony tunnels. Someone should look before Arasaka does.
A famous media wants to 'collaborate' on a prank. The Vampyres want a cut and a hostage clause.

name: Julliard Guild
turf: Downtown, the Glen, NCART stations, any street corner with an open case
look: Instrument cases with the guild sticker, performance clothes, a quiet pistol
origin: Night City buskers used to get robbed, recruited, or both. Julliard turned that into a closed shop. If you play on a corner in 2045, you are in the Guild or you are about to have a conversation about dues. They protect their stages the way Tyger Claws protect a den, just with better timing.
text: They are artists with a monopoly. Charisma is the weapon until it is not. They hate Bozos (chaos), feud with Philharmonic Vampyres (mimes), and can fill a plaza with a flash mob that is also a picket line. Shakespeare McBride runs it like a union that never heard of a strike fund because the strike is a brick.
hooks: A NCART busker refused the sticker. The Guild wants them in. The busker wants a bodyguard for one week.
A corpo wants 'authentic street music' for a launch and will not pay Guild rates. Shakespeare noticed.
A stolen violin is a Kendachi. The Guild wants it back before the Claws smell the steel.

name: Piranhas
turf: Pacifica Playground, Playland by the Sea, any party worth crashing
look: Club fashion, the shoal tattoo, too much chrome in the smile
leader: Corpse Reviver; the gang is split into shoals
origin: Night City's premiere party gang, and they will mug you on the way in. In 2020 they were already the 'just because' crew: drink, dance, rob, repeat. By 2045 they do not just attend the best nights. They throw them. Cells called shoals keep the brand alive without a single clubhouse the NCPD can bomb twice.
text: They ate ground from the 2045 Voodoo Boys posers and keep trying to swallow the Andersons. A Piranha gig is a plus-one that ends with a cybersnake. They are not ideological. They are hungry. If your table needs a crowd that becomes a combat, start here.
hooks: A shoal is throwing a party in Playland. The ticket is a job. The job is inside someone else's turf.
Corpse Reviver wants the Andersons absorbed, not murdered. Molly Anderson has other plans.
A stolen guest list from a corpo tower is circulating in a shoal. The tower will pay. So will the shoal.

name: Reckoners
turf: Hot Zone, the Glen, South Night City
look: Medallions of the Gibbering Eye, merch, a smile that is a donation plate
leader: The Beloved Gaping Maw of the Gibbering Eye
origin: A nihilist street church that preaches a coming Harvest of Souls and will take your wallet while they wait. They sell plushies. They sell tracts. They sell the idea that dying in the Hot Zone is a coupon. Night City has always grown cults in the cracks. This one learned merchandising.
text: They are funny until the stun baton. They proselytize, they roll unconscious bodies, they argue theology with a pop-up weapon. The Enhanced think cyberpsychosis is evolution. Reckoners think the void is a product line. Do not leave them alone with a wounded teammate.
hooks: A Glen landlord wants the medallion preachers off his stoop without a hate-crime headline.
The Maw's lieutenant is skimming donations. The Maw wants a quiet audit.
A plushie in a kid's bag has a tracker. Follow it.

name: Gold Dragons
turf: Little China
look: Puffy gold jackets, jump boosters, grip feet, Hong Kong-action posing
leader: Edwina "Eddy" Sing, under city manager David Ling Po
origin: Little China's other government needed a visible fist. Ling Po — parlor, office, the whole doubled life — put Eddy Sing in gold and told her to make the district look like a movie. The Dragons took the brief literally: honor codes from old discs, wire-fu chrome, protection that is also a tax.
text: They are a guardian gang with a poser streak. They will catch you off a fire escape because the jump booster made it pretty. Tyger Claws have opinions. Maelstrom has appetites. The Dragons hold the middle by looking expensive and hitting like stunt people who rehearse.
hooks: Eddy Sing wants a Red Chrome cell walked out of Little China on camera, not in a bag.
Ling Po hires the party for a job the Dragons cannot be seen doing. Guess which kind.
A gold jacket was stripped off a dead kid who was not a Dragon. Eddy wants the thief more than the jacket.

name: Albino Alligators
turf: Rancho Coronado car-wash ruin, South Night City's Hen House
look: Black polos with a white cartoon gator toting a rifle — the last print run of a dead car wash
leader: Big Bruno, with Tarquin under him
origin: They found a pile of promotional shirts in an abandoned car wash and decided that was a mythology. Poser gang, small, armed, and currently being pushed out of the neighborhood by locals and mercs who are tired of the bit. Night City is full of crews that started as a joke. Some stay funny. The Alligators bought rifles.
text: They want to be a real gang. Rancho keeps telling them no. Bruno is loud. Sin Gin watches the lot. If they survive the year it will be because someone hired them as disposable color.
hooks: Bruno wants the car wash recognized as turf. The block association will pay to keep the hoses dry.
A mer group already ran them off once. The Alligators want a rematch with rented legends.
The last box of original shirts is in a Biotechnica storage unit. Bruno will pay stupid money.

name: The Andersons
status: Active, aging, in danger of being eaten by Piranhas
turf: Old Combat Zone, Playland by the Sea
look: Denim, ANDERSON tattooed across both sets of knuckles
leader: Molly Anderson — yogang boss and rising fixer
origin: A family-themed yogang that got old without getting a pension. They mug, scav, and run Night Markets in the Old Combat Zone because Molly turned a street name into a brand. The Piranhas smell weakness. Molly smells a Night Market stall with better lighting.
text: They are kids who named themselves after a sitcom family and then had to live in a war ruin. Molly is the reason they still exist. She is also the reason a crew of edgerunners might get a real gig instead of a turf funeral.
hooks: Molly needs stall security for a Combat Zone Night Market. Piranhas RSVP'd themselves.
A knuckle tattoo walks into the Forlorn Hope asking for work. Molly says they are not hers.
Playland wants the Andersons off the pier. Molly wants a counteroffer.

name: Arzin Tynon
turf: New Westbrook, Watson Development, the northern edge
look: Armorjacks with the mark on the back, 20th-century biker cosplay with real engines
origin: An old boostergang that never got the message that Night City moved on from choppers. They smuggle, deal, race, extort, and throw random violence like it is a seasoning. In 2020 they were already in the books. In 2045 they are still on the northern rim, still louder than the law.
text: Biker culture as a combat style. Skinweave, shotguns, roadbikes, a leader who thinks the 1900s are a personality. They will race you, then rob you, then tell you it was the same event.
hooks: Dequiallo wants a Dragula Racers hearse beaten in a night race. Cheating is expected. Getting caught is not.
A smuggling run from Watson Development needs a second set of guns that is not Maelstrom.
NCPD is too scared to ticket a funeral ride. A widow is not. She will pay.

name: Culper Ring
turf: NorCal Military Base, rumored South Night City safehouses
look: Nothing obvious — a mark in jewelry or under a sleeve, COG uniforms by day
origin: A secret sect inside the Estero Bay Military COG that wants NorCal back in the United States the old-fashioned way: spies, rifles, and patience. They are combat trained because most of them already have a duty roster. Night City street kids will never see them. Edgerunners who take a 'patriotic' gig might.
text: Not a booster gang. A conspiracy with a logo. If your table likes midnight meetings and the chance that the client is wearing a real rank, this is the file. They are not here to mug a kiosk.
hooks: A COG lieutenant wants a data slate from Night Corp without a paper trail.
Someone in the party used to serve. A ring member recognizes the unit tattoo and makes an offer.
A South Night City safehouse burned. The Ring thinks it was NUSA. It might have been 6th Street playing dress-up.

name: DeadWoods
turf: The Glen, South Night City, trains and railyards
look: Cowboy hats in 2045, dusters, targeting optics they pretend are just eyes
origin: A cowboy poser gang that appointed itself the railroad's guardian. They extort, gamble, sell companionship, and actually do keep some of the cargo moving because a dead rail line is a dead bit. They run The Molly May, a casino in the Glen, which is the closest thing they have to a ranch house.
text: Sandevistan cowboys. They will quote a western and then pull a pistol that does not care about quotes. Useful on a train. Loud in a city. The Steel Vaqueros think they are tourists. The DeadWoods think the Vaqueros are the help.
hooks: A cargo train is being bled by Toecutters. Hurston will pay for a posse that can stay on a moving car.
The Molly May's tables are running hot with a cheater who is also a netrunner.
A Glen landlord wants the casino's 'security' to stop looking like a hanging.

name: The Dirty Hippies
turf: Rancho Coronado, University District
look: Faded tie-dye, guns under the peace print, dirt under the nails that is actually product
origin: Guerrilla gardeners who grow weeds and herbs laced with whatever the week is selling, collectively called ganga. The name is a joke they do not live up to. They do not believe in peace. They believe in botany and a pistol.
text: They will sell you a calm and then shoot the cop who followed you. University kids think they are a vibe. Rancho thinks they are a zoning violation with automatic fire.
hooks: Canary's crop was sprayed by Biotechnica 'by accident.' She wants a greenhouse camera's memory.
A University dealer cut ganga with something that kills. The Hippies want the cutter more than NCPD does.
A community garden is real. The Hippies are using it as cover. The gardeners have started to notice the night shifts.

name: Dragula Racers
turf: Watson Development street circuits
look: Monster bodysculpts, hearses with NOS, racing numbers painted like grave markers
origin: Largely harmless by Night City standards, which still means people die on the course. They sculpt themselves into movie monsters and race hot-rod hearses. Frankie Sparks currently owns the street-racing scene the way a good driver owns a corner.
text: Hire them for a ride, a race, or a funeral that needs to arrive first. Do not hire them for a firefight unless the firefight is on wheels. Arzin Tynon wants their crown. The Racers want another lap.
hooks: Frankie will throw a race if the party can guarantee a corp spectator gets humiliated, not killed.
A hearse is carrying an actual body someone wants to steal mid-race.
Maelstrom thinks a racer's chrome is 'wasted on a costume.' A challenge was issued.

name: The Enhanced
turf: Possibly Heywood Industrial Zone and South Night City; they prefer not to be found
look: The mark branded or etched into chrome. No uniform. That is the uniform.
origin: A cult that decided cyberpsychosis is not a disease. It is the next human. They are invested in GunMart — cheap weapons flooding the street so violence becomes weather — and they would rather detonate than be questioned. Street rumor says the Maelstrom of 2077 is what the Enhanced were aiming at in 2045.
text: You will not get a sit-down. You will get a philosophy lecture from a person who is already halfway gone, or you will get a bomb. They promote megaviolence the way a corp promotes a product line: volume, price, ubiquity.
hooks: A GunMart crate is being diverted to a South Night City cell. Militech will pay. So will the Enhanced, in bullets.
A cyberpsycho break has the Enhanced's mark on the remaining metal. MaxTac wants a consultant who is not a cop.
Someone in the party is slipping. An Enhanced recruiter noticed first.

name: Eurotrashers
turf: Little Europe
look: 1980s European fashion as imagined by someone who has never been, plus an unplaceable accent
origin: A Little Europe party gang that mugs with a blackjack more often than a rifle, until the Undertow shows up. They are posers of a continent. The accent is a bit. The knives are not.
text: Useful as local color and as a street fight that starts over a look. They hate the Undertow's greaser nostalgia because there is only so much room on one boulevard for two decades that never happened.
hooks: Refrain wants an Undertow greaser walked out of a Little Europe club without gunfire.
A fake accent hid a real Euro corp kid on the run. Both gangs want the bounty.
A blackjack artist from the gang is better than they should be. Someone trained them.

name: Fixie's Couriers
turf: Heywood Industrial Zone and every sidewalk that will take a bike
look: Reflective caps and arm bands, cyberlegs, a package you do not open
leader: Fixie — a fixer who guides, not a general who orders
origin: Half the small-package economy of Night City on two wheels. They are a gang the way a union is a gang: shared risk, shared routes, a boss who is also the dispatcher. You do not mug a courier twice.
text: If your table needs a faction that knows every alley and hates surprise inspections, this is it. They will carry a soul or a sandwich. The rate changes. The legs do not stop.
hooks: A package is ticking. Fixie wants it delivered anyway, and a team to make sure the destination is the right sin.
Maelstrom is taxing a bike route. The couriers will pay for a week of fear in the other direction.
A courier vanished in H4. The Rat Kings know why.

name: G3
turf: Kabuki, Watson Development
look: Anime-themed bodysculpt, J-pop fashion, too much chrome around the eyes
origin: A disturbingly violent anime poser gang that also runs 100.0 G3 Gun-Gal, a Kabuki radio station. They pirate discs, talk shop, and then commit random violence like it is a transformation sequence. Many members are close to cyberpsychosis and do not treat that as a problem.
text: Cute until the very heavy melee. Tyger Claws share Kabuki and find them embarrassing, which is not the same as safe. If a radio drop sounds like a hit announcement, it might be.
hooks: Hazumi wants a pirate archive pulled off a corp shard before a Claw lawyer does.
A G3 sculpt job went wrong. The ripper wants muscle when the family comes.
Gun-Gal accidentally broadcast a real assassination. The station needs the file gone and the listener quiet.

name: Generation Red
turf: Old Combat Zone
look: A logo patch somewhere on the clothes, scavenged everything else
origin: A Combat Zone yogang that survived a Kill Krasher invasion of their clubhouse and accidentally impressed both ERI (the Zone's nominal government) and Danger Gal. They are kids. They are resourceful. They are one bad night from a documentary or a funeral.
text: Hire them as local guides. Do not hire them as a war. Apex knows the difference. Carrion of the Kill Krashers does not.
hooks: Apex wants the party to sit in on a Danger Gal meeting so the kids are not eaten by a contract.
Kill Krashers are coming back for the clubhouse. Generation Red has paint, not anti-armor.
ERI offers the gang a 'charter.' The fine print is a leash.

name: Kill Krashers
turf: Southern Island, with raids into the Combat Zone
look: Black and red painted rippers
origin: A new crew that glorifies violence as the whole personality. Small numbers are a bar fight. Large numbers are a weather event. They hit Generation Red's clubhouse and learned the kids bite. They did not learn to stop.
text: No ideology, no turf pride, just the next broken thing. If your table needs a gang that does not negotiate, put red rippers on them and start the clock.
hooks: Carrion called a 'gathering' in the Glen. NCPD will not show. A landlord will pay.
A Krasher wants out after the clubhouse raid. Carrion does not do out.
Someone is arming them. Follow the grenades.

name: Lightning Cats
turf: The Hot Zone, wreck of the Old Med Center
look: Feline exotic bodysculpt, rippers, the choice to live 'wild'
origin: Cat-themed exotics who decided the Old Med Center ruins were a habitat. They talk about not being corporate housepets. They train martial arts and cyberweapons like they mean the metaphor with claws.
text: Hot Zone survivalists with a look. They will trade. They will hunt. They will not take kibble for an answer. Useful allies if you can stand the bit. Bad enemies in a vertical ruin.
hooks: Bengal Khan wants a Biotechnica animal vault mapped, not raided. Yet.
A Cat took a job in the city and did not come back. The pack does not do missing-person quietly.
Scavvers are stripping the Med Center. The Cats consider that poaching.

name: Mudang Gumi
turf: Pacifica Playground and the CitiNet
look: Unknown on purpose
origin: Netrunners and thieves who do not do parades. Espionage, identity theft, CitiNet scams. Motivations classified even to the people writing the street files. If Tanson is in the picture, this is a corp war in a gang costume.
text: The anti-Maelstrom. No optics to catch the light. A data thief with Interface 4 and a grapple gun. If your table's netrunner is getting hunted by someone polite, start here.
hooks: A stolen identity is wearing a party member's face on a loan document.
Tanson denies the Gumi. A dead drop in Pacifica disagrees.
The Gumi will pay in clean identities for a physical smash-and-grab they cannot do from a chair.

name: The Muses
turf: Woodland Park in North Heywood; Xanadu derby arena / club
look: Togas, disco, big hair, roller skates, color-shift eyes
origin: A poser gang that mixed 1980s gloss with a costume-shop Greece and then became an actual roller derby squad in the Wonderland League. They party. They skate. They hit. Xanadu is theirs.
text: Do not laugh at the toga in the rink. Combat awareness 4 on skates is a traffic accident with choreography. They will hire muscle to keep Xanadu's door from becoming someone else's.
hooks: A derby grudge against a Street Queen is about to leave the rink.
Xanadu's night is being taxed by 6th Street. Calliope wants a message that still lets veterans drink.
A Muse's color-shift eyes were stolen off her face. Scavs. She wants them back in the socket they came from.

name: Prime-Time Players
turf: New Westbrook, Upper Marina
look: Sitcom and old-television bodysculpts, costumes that are a little too accurate
origin: Posers who pick a show and become it, then split into factions when the fandom does. Extortion, companionship, blackmail, and the occasional laugh-track beating. Night City has always made people into products. These people volunteered.
text: Useful as a disguise economy. Dangerous as a blackmail economy. Vang keeps the factions from murdering each other on set by pointing them at civilians instead.
hooks: A 'family sitcom' faction is shaking down a Marina block. The block wants the season cancelled.
A stolen master tape of a dead show is worth a killing. Vang will pay more than the collector.
Someone sculpted themselves into a party member's mother. It is not a compliment.

name: Princesses of Justice
turf: University District; Princessland, an abandoned traveling amusement park
look: Magical-girl / animated-heroine sculpt and costume, very heavy melee
origin: A poser gang based on an old animated show that decided the bit should save people. They shelter victims of domestic abuse in a dead amusement park and will cave in a skull to keep the gate shut. Guardian gang in a pastel wrapper.
text: Do not mock the costume in Princessland. They have Kevlar and a reason. University cops ignore them. Abusers do not get to.
hooks: Someone followed a client to Princessland. Adorable wants the follower lost, not famous.
A corp wants to 'redevelop' the park. The Princesses want a delay measured in broken dozers.
A kid in the colors is a poser tourist. The real crew wants them unmasked before an abuser uses the confusion.

name: Rat Kings
turf: Megabuilding H4, Santo Domingo, still under construction
look: Logo on the jacket, the building's dust on everything else
origin: A small boostergang using an unfinished megabuilding as a dungeon crawl they live in. They party, steal, mug, vanish into the guts of H4, and let the structure be the alibi.
text: If your map is a half-built tower, they are the wandering monsters. Corona thinks that is a strategy. It is. Until the tower opens and NCPD invents a lobby.
hooks: A Fixie's courier disappeared between floors 20 and 40. The Kings know which dark.
IEC wants the construction site cleared without a massacre headline.
Corona will sell a route through H4. The route is also an ambush. Both things can be true.

name: The Shroomers
turf: Tunnels under the Old Combat Zone
look: Specialized low-light optics, a token you do not fake, dirt that is a farm
origin: Part survivalist family, part guerrilla farm. They grow fungi in the dark under the Combat Zone and send eighteen-year-olds up top for a Wander Year to see if the city is worth returning from. Most come back. Some come back wrong. Some do not come back.
text: They will trade food that is not kibble. They will not give you a map of the tunnels. A Shroomer token in your pocket is a passport or a death sentence depending on who sees it.
hooks: A Wander Year kid is dying in a Santo clinic and will not talk to NCPD. May will.
Something is eating the farms from below. It is not a rival gang.
A corpo wants the strain. Pa would rather burn the beds.

name: The Sinful Adams
turf: South Night City Boneyard
look: Goth fashion, a community that shares food and school with refugees
origin: A goth poser gang that accidentally became a government for people living in the Boneyard. They share housing, meals, even lessons. Gomez keeps the lights on. Ophelia keeps the lights from being stolen.
text: Not a joke if you live there. A mercenary job against the Adams is a job against a neighborhood. Street Queens might get along with them. Toecutters will not.
hooks: Ophelia needs guns for a Toecutter raid that Gomez does not want to admit is coming.
A Boneyard school is out of filters. A Biotechnica crate would fix it. Stealing it starts a clock.
A media wants a human-interest piece. Gomez wants the cameras pointed anywhere else.

name: Steel Vaqueros
turf: New Westbrook, Rancho Coronado, the west-coast road when they are on it
look: The pack mark on the jacket, nomad chrome, bikes that have seen Chile and Seattle
origin: A nomad pack that never joined a nation. They run the coast, recruit locals as junior members to hold the fort, and smuggle whatever the road will bear. Unaffiliated means no Aldecaldo court when they screw up. It also means no nation war when they don't.
text: Hire them to move a thing. Do not hire them to sit still. DeadWoods think they own the rails. The Vaqueros think rails are a suggestion.
hooks: Ximena needs a local crew to hold a Westbrook safehouse for three weeks while the pack is south.
A junior member sold a route to Wraiths. The pack is not in town. The party is.
CHOOH2 cut with water killed an engine on the freeway. The Vaqueros want the station owner.

name: The Street Queens
turf: New Westbrook, Upper Marina, the mainland underground clubs
look: Queer iconography as jewelry, club clothes, rippers
origin: A guardian gang for queer Night City: doors, neighborhoods, the clubs that would not exist if someone else held the door. They also have a hand in the drug and sex economies of those same rooms, because protection that cannot pay rent is a eulogy.
text: Allies of the Mox in spirit, older in the 2045 books. They will hire edgerunners who understand the difference between a raid and a rescue. They will not hire tourists.
hooks: A Marina club's door was hit by 6th Street 'vice.' Maxine wants the veterans to feel unwelcome, not martyred.
A Queen is missing after a Tyger Claw night. Kabuki cameras lie. People do not, if you ask hard.
Prime-Time Players used a Queen's face as a costume. Maxine wants the sculpt gone.

name: The Toecutters
turf: North Heywood edges, the Outskirts
look: Nomad leathers with blood-spatter patterns that are not an accident
origin: A Raffen Shiv clan on Night City's rim. The rumor is they cut toes and make a meal of the lesson. The rumor is the point. Smuggling and violence with a side of folklore that keeps civilians on the freeway.
text: Wraiths of an earlier decade's name. If a convoy goes quiet north of Heywood, start here. Do not expect a speech.
hooks: A Nomad kid crawled into Vista del Rey missing pieces. 6th Street wants revenge they are not trained for.
A smuggler used Toecutter roads without paying. The invoice is a person.
Someone is wearing blood-spatter leather as fashion in the Glen. That will be corrected.

name: Tombstone Preservers
turf: Anywhere the dead are washed, prayed over, or planted
look: Shaved heads, excellent suits, martial calm
origin: A guardian gang that decided the dead were the last clients who could not pay extra. They keep mortuaries, graves, and body banks from becoming scav buffets. Each member is a fighter. The suit is the uniform and the warning.
text: Scavs hate them. Trauma Team respects them. Families hire them. If a funeral in your campaign needs security that is not 6th Street, call Rieper.
hooks: A body bank is buying from scavs again. The Preservers want a door broken and a ledger taken.
A corpo funeral is a hit waiting to happen. Rieper will hire specialists for the parts that are not solemn.
Someone buried a data shard in a chest cavity. The Preservers noticed the extra weight.

name: The Undertow
turf: Downtown
look: 1950s greaser fashion, more attitude than tactics
origin: Hotheads who want Downtown to stay 'real' against the Chamber of Commerce. They have no plan, no patience, and a lot of pomade. Eurotrashers fight them because the boulevard is only so wide.
text: Comic relief until someone dies on a zebra crossing. Rydell will hire anyone who looks like they have a plan. He will then ignore the plan.
hooks: The Chamber wants a greaser rally to fail without martyrs. Rydell wants martyrs.
A corpo restoration of a diner is actually a Night Corp sensor nest. The Undertow smashed the wrong diner.
Refrain of the Eurotrashers offers a truce. It is a setup. Everyone knows. Someone still has to go.

name: Wild Things
turf: Watson Development; the Redline bloodsport club
look: The mark branded or scarred into the chest, pit-fighter chrome
origin: A boostergang that put its violence in a cage and sold tickets. The Redline in Watson Development is their church. They also do mercenary work and the companionship economy for people who like bruises. They were already in the 2020 lists. They got better at the show.
text: Animals without the 2077 mall. If you need a gladiator, a bodyguard who looks like a problem, or a night that ends with a stretcher, Jenny Nails will quote you.
hooks: The Redline's champ was juiced by a corp. Jenny wants the corp intern who signed the vial.
A fight is fixed. The other fixer is Maelstrom. The Wild Things do not fix fights.
A branded kid is underage. Jenny wants them out of the building before NCPD invents a conscience.

name: Willows
status: Active (therapy group that can still kill you)
turf: From the Ashes clinic, Old Combat Zone, monthly
look: A challenge coin. No colors. That is the point.
origin: Female combat veterans who meet once a month at a Combat Zone clinic. Rogue has been seen. Trace Santiago was told not to call them a gang. They are a support group with a body count in the résumé column. Night City still files them here because the form has no box for 'people who got help and stayed armed.'
text: Do not start a fight in From the Ashes. Do not recruit their patients into 6th Street. Do not put their names in a media piece. If they hire you, it is because the job would look like a relapse if they did it themselves.
hooks: Ingénue wants a stalking corpo scared, not killed. Several Willows are famous enough that killing him would make news.
6th Street is leafleting the clinic. The coin-carriers want the leaflets to stop without a war.
A Willow missed two meetings. Her stack was tossed. The party is the welfare check with guns.

name: Yellow Brick Road Gang
turf: Night City's fantasy-themed corners and a brick road that is paint
look: Oz cosplay taken as far as chrome and cruelty will go
leader: Street file incomplete — they prefer the bit to a press kit
origin: A poser crew that picked a children's road and walked it into a city that eats children. Wizard, scarecrow, tin — the costumes change, the mugging does not. They are in the 2045 guide because someone kept surviving the encounter.
text: Harmless until the flying-monkey chrome. Useful as a parade that is also a pickpocket line. Prime-Time Players consider them competition. Children consider them a warning.
hooks: A 'wizard' sold a kid a real gun. The Queens and the Princesses both want a word.
The painted road is covering a Night Corp survey line. Someone wants the paint gone. Someone else wants the survey.
A tin-man sculpt job locked up in the rain. The ripper who did it is hiding.

name: The Zoners
turf: Old Combat Zone as identity, not just address
look: Zone salvage fashion, the pride of people who never left the fire
leader: Local captains; ERI would like to be in charge and is not
origin: Not every Combat Zone kid joined Generation Red or the Sights. Zoners are the ones who made the ruin itself the colors. They know the rubble. They tax the rubble. They die in the rubble and call it home.
text: Guides, ambushes, and a chip on the shoulder aimed at anyone with a clean jacket. If your campaign lives in the Zone, you will pay them or fight them. Often both.
hooks: A Zoner map of the tunnels is for sale. The Shroomers say it is a lie. It might be a trap. It might be both.
ERI wants a Zoner captain at a table. The captain wants a hostage first.
Maelstrom is recruiting in the Zone. The Zoners will sell the recruiters out for ammo.

name: Crawling Cobras
turf: Night City's wet edges and the kind of club that keeps snakes
look: Reptile sculpt, cobra iconography, slow walks that are a threat display
leader: Street file thin; they prefer rumor to interviews
origin: A 2045 booster/poser hybrid that took the snake as a whole personality: patience, venom, the long wait under a floorboard. They show up in the RED lists because enough bodies turned up with puncture patterns that were not animals.
text: Not the Lightning Cats' cousins, though a tourist might think so. Cobras wait. Cats hunt. If a deal feels too quiet, check the ceiling.
hooks: A night market stall is paying a 'snake tax.' The stall wants it to end without a panic.
A Cobra sculpt went feral in a club. The club is Tyger Claw. Diplomacy is a stretcher.
Someone is selling fake venom as smash. The Cobras consider that a copyright issue.

name: Desperados
turf: Overlapping the DeadWoods' cowboy circuit, with less railroad and more wanted posters
look: Outlaw western, not guardian western
leader: Whoever is still standing after the last toast
origin: If DeadWoods are the sheriff show, Desperados are the other channel. Same century, opposite sermon. They rob, run, and pose for cameras that do not exist.
text: A posse you hire when you want the crime to look like a story. A problem when they believe the story.
hooks: Hurston of the DeadWoods wants a Desperado crew run off a Glen casino without a shootout on the felt.
A 'train robbery' is scheduled on a cargo line that has a Night Corp inspector aboard.
A Desperado left a calling card at a Valentino funeral. Padre is not a film fan.

name: Fabulous Mayhem
turf: Club circuit, wherever a night can be ruined on purpose
look: Glam, glitter, and a willingness to make the glitter a weapon
leader: A rotating queen of the night
origin: A party gang that treated chaos as choreography. They are on the 2045 list because the chaos kept having a body count. Street Queens sometimes share a dance floor with them. Sometimes they share a lawsuit.
text: Hire them to crash a corpo party. Do not hire them to be subtle. Mayhem is in the letterhead.
hooks: A corpo launch needs to fail as a meme, not a massacre. Mayhem will need a leash. The leash will fail.
Glitter turned out to be a tracking dust. The gang wants the supplier.
Maxine Raunch wants them out of a Queen's club for one weekend. She will pay in a favor that is not cash.

name: Hell's Angels
status: Active as a 20th-century name that Night City never managed to bury
turf: Highway clubs, northern bars, the idea of a run
look: The old colors, updated chrome, bikes that predate CHOOH2 and were converted anyway
origin: The 20th-century club survived into the Time of the Red the way cockroaches and corporations did: by not taking the hint. Night City chapters mixed with local booster culture until the name was both a historical costume and a real engine. Arzin Tynon stole the look. The Angels still have the lawyers, or the memory of lawyers.
text: Not a poser gang, they will tell you. The street files still file them next to posers because the century is a costume now. Do not say that on a run.
hooks: A chapter wants a CHOOH2 route that Petrochem 'forgot' to license.
Arzin Tynon wore a rocker that was not theirs. The Angels want it burned off a jacket, not a person. Maybe.
A veteran Angel is dying of old chrome. They want a night ride through a district that banned bikes.

name: High-Class Heist Crew
turf: Wherever the vault is
look: Evening wear, no colors, the opposite of a booster parade
leader: A planner who does not use a street name twice
origin: The 2045 books listed them as a gang because Night City lists anything that repeats a crime. They are a professional theft set: tuxedos, timing, and a getaway that is not a panzer. Maelstrom thinks they are cowards. They think Maelstrom is a noise complaint.
text: If your table wants Ocean's-whatever in 2045, this is the file. They will hire specialists. They will burn specialists. Read the contract twice.
hooks: A tower job needs a face the cameras have never seen. That is the party.
A heist went loud. The crew wants the person who brought a booster into a whisper job.
Arasaka lost something they will not name. The Heist Crew did not take it. They know who did.

name: Lost Kids
turf: Stacks, squats, the edges of yogang maps
look: Whatever still fits, a mark they invent every month
leader: Whoever can find food this week
origin: A yogang in the true sense: kids without houses who clustered so the street would have to eat them in a group. They are not successful. They are not supposed to be. Night City files them so GMs remember the Combat Zone has children in it.
text: Do not make them comic relief. Do not make them an army. A Lost Kid gig is a missing-person, a stolen blanket, a corp charity that is a trap.
hooks: A stack landlord is selling 'adoption' to a body bank. The Kids know the van.
Generation Red wants to take them in. Half the Kids think that is a gang. Half think that is a bed.
A media wants a documentary. The first camera already got someone killed.

name: Saturday Night Buttkickers
turf: Weekend fights, parking lots, the kind of bar that still has a jukebox
look: Disco-era fight fashion, bruises as membership cards
leader: The last one standing when the song ends
origin: A party/combat gang that treated Saturday like a holiday of fists. They are in the RED catalog because the parking-lot wars kept happening after the war that was supposed to end wars.
text: Wild Things with a calendar. Hire them for a brawl. Do not hire them for a Tuesday.
hooks: A bar in Santo wants one Saturday without a hospitalization. They will pay for a fake fight that ends early.
A Buttkicker crossed Animals in a 2077-era pit (if your table jumped decades) and did not walk out.
Someone is filming the lots for a BD. The gang wants a cut. The filmmaker wants blood.

name: Western Stars
turf: The cowboy circuit, media lots, the idea of a horizon
look: Cleaner western than DeadWoods, more camera-ready
leader: A front-person who can still ride
origin: 2020 poser royalty: the western as lifestyle brand. Some grew into DeadWoods. Some stayed Stars — the ones who wanted the poster, not the railroad. They still show up at parades and shootouts that were supposed to be pretend.
text: A media's idea of a gang. Sometimes that is cover for a real theft. Sometimes it is just a theft of taste.
hooks: A Stars parade is covering a Culper Ring pickup. The Stars do not know. The Ring is counting on that.
Hurston says they are diluting the bit. A duel was offered. The Stars want a second.
A stolen stallion is a genetically printed Biotechnica showpiece. It kicked a ganger and ran.

name: Metal Warriors
turf: Old Combat Zone (then)
look: Early full-borg booster fashion, the prototype of the red-eye look
leader: Dead, missing, or wearing a new name
origin: The boostergang the Inquisitors almost wiped off the map. They treated chrome as destiny a decade before Maelstrom made it a brand. Survivors, plus Iron Sights and Red Chrome leftovers, welded the whirlpool. If you find Metal Warrior colors in 2045, you have found a relic, a liar, or a Maelstrom history lesson.
text: Use them as ghosts. A cache of 2020 chrome. A survivor in a ripper's chair. A kid wearing a jacket they found. Maelstrom does not like museums.
hooks: A Combat Zone crate is stamped with a mark older than Maelstrom. Warlock wants it. An Inquisitor cell wants it burned.
A ganger claims the old name. Royce (or Warlock) will want a conversation.
A documentary crew is digging. They will not survive the premiere without help.

name: Blood Razors
status: Defunct in Night City; a splinter once held East Village in New York
turf: Combat Zone of the Mob Rule years; later a feared 2010s name
look: Blades, blood as advertising, the confidence of a crew that out-feared the Slaughterhouse
leader: Hack Man (2010s). The bounty on the Inquisitor boss was his.
origin: They rose during the Mob Rule (2005–2009) and spent the 2010s as one of Night City's most feared combat gangs, rivaled only by the Slaughterhouse. They hated Inquisitors with a personal heat: rumor said the Inquisitor leader killed Hack Man's brother. The 25,000 eb bounty did not end the war. Time, the Fourth Corporate War, and bigger whirlpools did. By RED they are a story you tell to scare boosters.
text: A table in 2020 can still step on them. A table in 2045 finds jackets, grudges, and maybe a New York cousin. Do not resurrect them as a joke. They earned the name.
hooks: The bounty chit is still in a safe. The name on it might still be breathing.
A Razor splinter in another city wants a relic from the Combat Zone. Maelstrom is using the relic as a doorstop.
An old woman in Heywood says Hack Man was her brother. She wants the Inquisitor story finished.

name: The Slaughterhouse
status: Defunct as a power; the name still empties a bar
turf: Combat Zone abattoirs and the blocks that smelled like them
look: Butcher chrome, aprons that were not a bit
leader: None living that the street will admit
origin: The other nightmare of 2010s Night City, matched only by the Blood Razors for sheer reputation. They made violence a workplace. The War and the nuke years finished the factory. 2045 kids use the name as a dare. 2020 tables can still walk into the kill floor.
text: Historical file with a smell. If you need a dungeon that used to be a gang, start in a building with drains in the floor.
hooks: A Santo meat plant is using Slaughterhouse marks as 'heritage branding.' Someone surviving from the old crew is not flattered.
A BD of the old floors is circulating. The people in it were not actors.
Scavs opened a sealed locker. The tools inside have names engraved.

name: Steel Slaughter Slammers
turf: Combat Zone circuits
look: Boostergang metal, slam culture, the long name that was a threat
origin: A 2020 combat crew whose name was the whole manifesto. They slammed, they steel'd, they did not make the Time of the Red as a going concern. Pieces of them walked into Maelstrom, the Sights, or a grave.
text: Use as a jacket in a closet, a tattoo on a 60-year-old drunk, a rivalry that only one person still remembers.
hooks: A Slammer jacket in a Night Market is tagged with a tracker. The buyer is already followed.
A ripper recognizes a 2020 serial in a 2045 ganger and wants the party to ask why.
Someone is restarting the name. Maelstrom will not share the letter S.

name: The D.J.'s
status: Defunct as a gang; the mix still exists
turf: Clubs, pirate towers, the idea of a night
look: Deck-first, gun-second, logos on records that scratch like knives
origin: A 2020 crew that treated the mix as turf. They fought over frequencies the way boosters fought over corners. Radio in 2045 is corporate or pirate. The D.J.'s were the prototype of both and the funeral of neither.
text: A historical file for tables that want a club war. G3's Gun-Gal is a grandchild that will not admit parentage.
hooks: A 2020 master disc is worth a killing in Kabuki. Hazumi Ihara will bid. So will a corpo nostalgia imprint.
A pirate tower still broadcasts a D.J.'s ident. The operator is dead. The automation is not.
Someone sampled a rival's kill on a track. The family heard it.

name: The Bradi Bunch
status: Defunct as a headline; family posers persist under other names
turf: Suburban ruins, the sitcom as a fortress
look: Matching family sculpt, the joke that had guns
origin: The textbook family poser gang of 2020: they copied a household, then defended the bit with firearms. The Andersons are what happens when that joke grows up in a Combat Zone and gets a fixer. The Bunch themselves are a 2020 encounter and a 2045 punchline.
text: Use in a 2020 game as written. Use in 2045 as the reason Molly Anderson does not smile when you mention sitcoms.
hooks: A Bunch survivor wants the Andersons to acknowledge a lineage. Molly does not.
A corpo 'family values' ad used their old look. The remaining members can still shoot.
A matching-sculpt cult in Rancho is not the Bunch. It is doing the Bunch better. That is worse.

name: The Brainiacs
turf: University edges, proto-NET cafes
look: Smartest-person-in-the-room fashion, decks that predate modern ice
origin: 2020's nerd gang: brains as a weapon, decks as a personality. Some of them died in the Old NET's collapse. Some of them became the reason Mudang Gumi has a reputation. The name did not survive. The habit did.
text: A historical netrunner club with street muscle on the payroll. 2045 tables meet their students and do not get the joke.
hooks: A Brainiac icebox from 2020 just pinged. It should not still have power.
A University ghost story is a real server. The Vampyres want it for a prank. The Gumi want it for theft.
A dead member's daughter has the old handle. She does not know what it opens.

name: Sacred Blades
status: Defunct as a gang; the draw lives in Claw dojos
turf: Japantown of the old map
look: Monoedge as religion, less syndicate than sect
leader: A sensei whose students joined other flags
origin: A 2020 blade cult/gang that treated the sword as a commandment. Tyger Claws out-organized them. Kendachi out-sold them. A few teachers still run rooms where you do not speak until you bow.
text: If you need a dojo that is not Claw property, this is the ghost on the lease.
hooks: A Sacred Blade kata is the unlock for a 2020 safe. The last student is dying.
Claws want the dojo's name erased. The sensei's grandchild will pay for a delay.
A Kendachi prototype was left as an offering. Both the company and the Claws felt it move.

name: The Gilligans
turf: Waterfront wrecks, a 'island' that was a pier
look: Castaway poser kit, worse ideas
origin: A 2020 poser gang that picked a shipwreck sitcom and moved it onto a toxic pier. They are a joke in the old books and a cautionary tale about picking the wrong bit in a city with tides that burn.
text: Use as a 2020 encounter on the docks. 2045: a rusted theme bar and a body in a skipper's hat.
hooks: A pier 'island' is still taxed by someone using the old name. The Piranhas want the dock.
A Biotechnica barrel washed up in their old lagoon. Do not open it. Someone will.
A media wants to reboot the bit. The water is still wrong.

name: Black Queens
status: Defunct as a flag; the work went into Street Queens and later the Mox
turf: Club doors of the old city
look: Queen iconography before it was jewelry-code
leader: A door that would not open
origin: A 2020 guardian/poser crew on the queer and club side of the map. The Street Queens of 2045 and the Mox of 2077 are not the same org chart, but the job did not change: hold the door, tax the room, bury your dead in the right clothes.
text: Historical sisters. A 2045 Queen might spit if you say they are a reboot. A 2077 Mox might not have heard the name. Both still do the work.
hooks: A Black Queen jacket in a Night Market has a list in the lining. Some names are still alive.
Maxine wants the list. Lizzie's people would want it too, if your table is in 2077.
A corpo Pride float used the old mark. The surviving members can still find a float.

name: Back Alley Brawlers
turf: Alleys, by definition
look: Tape, teeth, no theme except the win
origin: The 2020 name for people who fought in alleys for money before Wild Things put a cage around it and Animals put a mall around the cage. They did not need a logo. The alley was the logo.
text: A historical fight club. Use it to explain why Night City still has a Saturday that sounds like a riot.
hooks: A Brawler champion from 2020 is a ripper's skeleton with a belt. Someone wants the belt.
Jenny Nails found a Brawler rulebook. She wants a throwback night. The alley does not have insurance.
A kid is using the old name. The remaining drunks will test them.

name: Steel Dragons
turf: Highways, the go-gang map
look: Bikes, dragon motifs, speed as theology
leader: A rider whose name is a paint job now
origin: The typical 2020 go-gang in the old taxonomy: urban speed tribe, not always Japanese, always loud. Tyger Claws took the bikes and the city. Arzin Tynon took the American chopper half. The Dragons are a stripe on a tank that outlived the rider.
text: A chase scene with a history teacher. 2045 racers still steal their lines.
hooks: A dragon-painted bike in a Claw garage is a 2020 relic. The Claws do not know. A surviving Dragon does.
Frankie Sparks wants the old highway route for a hearse race. The route is a grave.
NCPD found a helmet with a map inside. The map still works. That is a problem.

name: Water Rats
turf: Harbor, storm drains, the toxic surf
look: Waders, rebreathers, chrome that rusts anyway
leader: A dock boss who learned to swim in acid
origin: A 2020 harbor gang: salvage, smuggling, bodies that float. Pacifica's later wrecks ate their map. Scavvers inherited the drains. A few Rats still know which outflow leads to a corp pipe.
text: If your table goes underwater in Night City, this is the old name for the people who already did.
hooks: A Rat chart of the drains is the only way into a Night Corp cistern.
Something in the harbor glows. The docks were not being poetic. A Rat will sell you a look.
IEC wants a tunnel mapped. The Rats want a reason to care.

name: Wire Cult
status: Defunct as a public cult; the theology went into the Enhanced and the Boys
turf: Old NET temples, cable basements
look: Wires as vestments, decks as altars
leader: A prophet who flatlined on purpose
origin: A 2020 net-cult that worshipped the connection itself. The collapse of the Old NET killed the church or scattered it into Voodoo Boys, Brainiacs, and the Enhanced. You can still find a basement with a circle of cables and a stain.
text: Historical horror. Do not play them as goofy. Play them as people who found a god in a server and it ate them.
hooks: A basement in Watson still answers ping. It should not.
A Wire Cult veve was painted over a Voodoo Boys mark. Pacifica will not like the plagiarism.
A party netrunner dreams in a voice that uses 2020 slang. The cult is not as dead as the file says.

name: The Trekkies
status: Defunct as a gang; fandom went home
turf: Convention ruins, University posers
look: Future-navy that was already retro in 2020
origin: A 2020 poser gang that took a 20th-century space opera as law. They are in the old lists. They did not survive contact with a city that had real orbital stations and nothing kind in them.
text: Comic until the phaser is a real microwaver. Use as 2020 color or a 2045 convention-murder.
hooks: A convention in the University District is using the old ranks. A real microwaver is in the prop box.
Orbital Air's marketing wants the look. The last Trekkie wants a lawyer or a gun.
A 'transporter accident' is a scav cover story.

name: The Elvises
status: Defunct as a unified poser army
turf: Nightclubs that still play the King
look: Too many jumpsuits, too many sideburns, chrome hips
origin: A 2020 poser gang of Elvis impersonators who treated the bit as a turf. Night City had the population to support a war of Kings. It did not have the patience. Prime-Time Players stole the method. The jumpsuits went to Night Markets.
text: A joke with a pistol in the belt. 2045 karaoke still starts fights that think they are history.
hooks: Two Elvises left. They have scheduled a duel in a Glen chapel. The Valentinos do not want sequins in the aisle.
A jumpsuit has a soulkiller fragment in the lining. No one knows why.
A corpo wants a hundred Elvises for a launch. There are not a hundred. There are Bozos who will try.

name: The Kennedys
turf: Media lots, poser politics
look: Dynasty hair, period suits, a smile for the camera and a gun for the alley
origin: A 2020 poser crew that copied an old American dynasty and then ran protection like a campaign. Culper Ring would later do the politics without the hair. The Kennedys did the hair without the country.
text: Use in 2020 as satire that shoots back. Use in 2045 as a costume box in a media warehouse.
hooks: A 'campaign event' in 2020 is a hit. The party is the security or the hit.
A 2045 media wants the last Kennedy for a reboot. The last Kennedy wants to stay buried.
A suit in a Night Market has a 2020 bug still transmitting. Someone is still listening.

name: Silver Slash
turf: Blade-and-chrome circuits of the old Zone
look: Silvered edges, slash marks as a calling card
origin: A 2020 combat gang that signed its work. They dueled, they marked, they lost the long war to bigger names. A slash on a 2045 door is either a copycat or a ghost.
text: Historical boosters with a handwriting. Useful as a signature at a crime scene that is older than the suspects.
hooks: A fresh silver slash appeared on a Claw door. The Claws want a name. The name might be a 70-year-old.
A blade in a Night Market has a Silver Slash serial. Kendachi says it is a fake. It cuts like it isn't.
A copycat is building a résumé. The remaining Slash, if any, is not flattered.

name: The Spikes
status: Defunct / folded into punk booster leftovers
turf: Old Combat Zone punk blocks
look: Spikes. On jackets, on chrome, on the problem.
origin: A 2020 booster/punk crew that made the fashion the weapon. Iron Sights outlasted them by getting a fixer. The Spikes outlasted themselves by not.
text: The missing link between 2013 street punk and 2045 BloodGuts. A jacket in a closet. A trap in an alley that still has a tripwire.
hooks: A Spike trap in the Zone just killed a Zoner. It was set in 2022. Someone re-armed it.
BloodGuts wants the old colors burned so the Sights are the only mohawk in the file.
A kid with a spiked jacket thinks it is fashion. The jacket has a tracker from a 2020 war.

name: Lords of Discipline
turf: Military-school ruins, 6th Street's older cousin in spirit
look: Uniform fetish, real surplus, a hierarchy that saluted itself
origin: A 2020 crew that played military academy in a city that had real veterans. 6th Street later did the veteran thing without the play. The Lords were the play without the war record. It did not save them.
text: A historical militia poser file. Use to shade 6th Street: this is what they look like to Valentinos.
hooks: A Lord of Discipline banner showed up at a 6th Street rally. X Wright wants it gone before the block laughs.
A surplus crate is stenciled with the old name. The guns still fire.
A 'colonel' is recruiting Lost Kids. The Willows will not allow it.

name: Fangs of Justice
turf: Vigilante rooftops of the old map
look: Hero costumes, real fangs, a press kit
origin: A 2020 vigilante poser gang: they wanted to be the Princesses of Justice before that show had a 2045 crew. They had fangs. They had a manifesto. They had a body count that was not always the right people.
text: Historical superheroes. The Princesses will not claim them. The Inquisitors might have hunted them for the fangs alone.
hooks: A Fangs mask in a museum heist is a real person's death mask. The museum does not know.
Adorable of the Princesses found a Fangs manifesto in Princessland. She wants it burned before the kids read the wrong chapter.
A copycat is 'saving' University students. The students did not ask.

name: Chrome Angels
turf: Full-borg parade routes
look: Wings in metal, halos in neon, boosters who thought they were icons
leader: A seraph with a linear frame
origin: A 2020 poser/booster hybrid: angels as chrome. Maelstrom made the chrome without the wings. Inquisitors made the theology without the glitter. The Angels lost both arguments.
text: A beautiful corpse of a gang. Use as a 2020 set piece or a 2045 statue that still has a power lead.
hooks: A Chrome Angel frame is in a body bank. It still tries to fly.
An Inquisitor cell wants the statue melted. A media wants it in a lobby.
A kid sculpted wings. Maelstrom offered a real pair. The kid should not take either deal.

name: Blue Angels
turf: Aerial poser circuit, rooftop clubs
look: Flight suits, cheap jump boosters, a sky they did not own
origin: Not the 20th-century navy team. A 2020 gang that stole the name and jumped off buildings. Most of the file is obituaries. Gold Dragons later did jump boosters with a district behind them.
text: A warning about names you cannot afford. Eddy Sing will not appreciate the comparison.
hooks: A Blue Angel jump route is still the fastest way off a tower. The last jumper missed.
Orbital Air wants the name killed in court. The gang is already dead. The merch is not.
A Gold Dragon was called a Blue Angel as an insult. Someone is in a dumpster.

name: Golden Knights
turf: Armor poser blocks
look: Gold-painted armorjack, knight bit, real maces
origin: A 2020 poser combat gang: medieval gold in a city of guns. They lost to firearms, fashion, and time. Gold Dragons later made gold jackets cool without the horse.
text: A 2020 joust in a parking structure. 2045: a helmet in a Night Market that still has blood in the lining.
hooks: Eddy Sing is not related. A Knight descendant wants a meeting anyway.
A corpo renaissance faire hired the look. The maces were real.
A golden armorjack is milspec under the paint. Militech wants it back.

name: The Morks
turf: University posers, alien-bit clubs
look: Red jumpsuits, rainbow suspenders as a threat display
